rationale: Attempt-00 (32x64x32,3 stages) passed and reached simulated_us=147.72; attempt-01 (32x64x64,2 stages) passed at 147.67, a marginal simulator-only improvement (not hardware measured; Metal ran exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binary not executed). Both kept block_N=64 despite attempt-01 prioritizing traffic, indicating footprint/compile pressure offsets the traffic gain, so we retain block_N=64 and block_N=128 to test widening under the 32768-byte cap. M=32 forces block_M=32 (64/128 do not divide M), so domain narrowed to [32]; other domains all remain nonempty and feasible: worst stage term 2*64*(32+128)*3=61440 exceeds cap, so HiGHS will avoid those tuples, while block_K=32/num_stages<=3 and block_N=128/stages=1 fit within the 32768 cap and the 4*block_M*block_N=16384 epilogue floor. Weights: traffic and pipeline raised to 2 to favor larger block_N and deeper pipelining that should cut the dominant 1/block_N traffic and per-iteration overhead for tall-skinny GEMM; launches and footprint lowered to 0.25 since N/block_N launches are already small and the 32-wide M limits tile area. Next hypothesis: test block_N=128 with num_stages=1/2 and block_K=32/64 to see if the wider tile reduces simulator latency within the shared cap; if footprint dominates again, narrow block_N back to [64] and increase block_K. No global-optimality claim is made.
